title: Panzanella
subtitle: Tuscan bread and tomato salad
excerpt: The great Tuscan summer salad: stale bread soaked in water and then squeezed out, tossed with ripe tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, basil, and a sharp red wine vinegar dressing. A lesson in doing nothing to good ingredients.

recipe.sourceNotes: Panzanella is a Florentine and broadly Tuscan salad that, like pappa al pomodoro, makes use of stale bread. The traditional recipe calls for moistening the stale bread in water (or water and vinegar) then squeezing it dry to break it into coarse chunks — a technique that gives the bread a specific sponge-like texture quite unlike toasted croutons. The dish is a product of the summer months when tomatoes are ripe and the kitchen needs to be kept cool. There is debate about whether the classic recipe includes cucumber (Florentine purists sometimes object) but the version with cucumber is the most widely made. Red onion is soaked in cold water to mellow its sharpness before being added raw. The dressing is simply red wine vinegar and extra-virgin olive oil.

content.text: Use the ripest possible tomatoes and the best olive oil you have. The bread must be stale and dense; fresh bread turns to glue. Soak the red onion in cold water for 15 minutes to mellow its raw bite before adding. Let the assembled salad sit for 20 minutes before serving so the bread absorbs the tomato juices and the dressing.

items.preparation: stale ciabatta or country loaf, torn into chunks; crusts left on
ripe; cut into irregular chunks, juices reserved
very thinly sliced; soaked in cold water for 15 minutes and drained

content.text: Soak the bread chunks in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until they have absorbed the water and are soft but not falling apart. Squeeze out firmly in your hands so the bread is moist but not dripping. Break into coarse, irregular pieces and place in a large bowl.
Add the tomatoes and all their juices, cucumber, drained red onion, capers, and basil to the bread. Drizzle over the vinegar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently to combine.
Leave to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving so the bread absorbs the tomato juices and the flavours meld. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve at room temperature; do not refrigerate.
